s: What was India's Global Innovation Index rank in 2025?
x: India ranked 38th of 139 in GII 2025, up from 39th in 2024 and 40th in 2022.

s: In which year was India ranked 52nd in the Global Innovation Index?
x: India was 52nd in 2019; it was 66th in 2016 and 81st in 2015.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Global Innovation Index?
o: It has 5 input and 2 output pillars
It is published by NITI Aayog
x: GII is published by WIPO, with 5 input and 2 output pillars; NITI Aayog publishes the India Innovation Index.

s: What was India's rank in the Network Readiness Index 2024?
x: India ranked 49th in the Network Readiness Index 2024, up from 79th in 2019.

s: Which of the following is a category in the India Innovation Index?
x: The categories are Major States, North-East and Hill States, and Union Territories and City States.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: India Innovation Index 2021, Major States leader – Manipur
India Innovation Index 2021, North-East and Hill States leader – Karnataka
India Innovation Index 2021, North-East and Hill States leader – Assam
x: The Global Innovation Index is published by WIPO. In the India Innovation Index 2021 Karnataka led the Major States and Manipur led the North-East and Hill States.

s: Which body publishes the India Innovation Index?
x: NITI Aayog publishes it with the Institute for Competitiveness; WIPO publishes the GII.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank among Major States in the India Innovation Index 2021?
x: AP was 9th among Major States (score 13.32); Telangana was 2nd.

s: Which UT/City State led the India Innovation Index 2021 in its category?
x: Chandigarh led the UTs and City States category in 2021.

s: Which State topped the 'Major States' category of the India Innovation Index 2021?
x: Karnataka led the Major States; Telangana was 2nd and Andhra Pradesh 9th.

s: Which State led the 'North-East and Hill States' category of the India Innovation Index 2021?
x: Manipur led the North-East and Hill States category in the 2021 index.

s: Which State ranked second among Major States in the India Innovation Index 2021?
x: Karnataka was first and Telangana second among Major States; Andhra Pradesh was 9th.

s: For how many years does the Patents Act, 1970 give patent protection?
x: Patents under the 1970 Act last 20 years; the invention must be novel with commercial application.

s: What is the slogan of the National IPR Policy, 2016?
o: Make in India; Innovate in India
x: The National IPR Policy, 2016 slogan is 'Creative India; Innovative India'.

s: Under which scheme is free IP filing facilitation provided for start-ups?
x: SIPP 2016 gives free start-up IP filing facilitation.

s:
Consider the following statements about patent filings in India:
1. In January-March 2022, Indian applicants filed more patent applications than foreign applicants.
2. This happened for the first time in 11 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: In January-March 2022, Indian applicants filed 10,706 applications against 9,090 by foreign applicants, the first time in 11 years.

s: What is India's global rank in scientific publications?
x: India ranked third globally in scientific publications; its nanoscience publications also ranked third after China and the USA.

s: What was India's position in global patent filing activity according to WIPO 2023 data?
x: India ranked sixth in the world in patent filing activity according to WIPO 2023.

s: India had approximately how many full-time-equivalent researchers per million people?
x: India had approximately 262 FTE researchers per million people.

s: IIITDM Kurnool in Andhra Pradesh has which of the following statuses?
o: State Council of Science and Technology
x: IIITDM Kurnool is an Institute of National Importance. It is not a CSIR laboratory, a DBT autonomous institute, or a state S&T council like APCOST.

s: How many PhDs were awarded in India in 2021-22?
x: 32,588 PhDs were awarded in 2021-22, the most in Science (7,408).

s: Which Andhra Pradesh institution ranked 20th among Indian institutions in the Nature Index 2026?
x: IISER Tirupati was 20th among Indian institutions in Nature Index 2026.

s: What was India's Gross Expenditure on Research and Development (GERD) as a percentage of GDP in FY 2023-24?
x: India's GERD was 0.84% of GDP in FY 2023–24, described as a 15-year high after reversing a decade-long decline.

s: Which country has the world's highest GERD as a percentage of GDP (about 6.3% in 2023)?
x: Israel spends about 6.3% of GDP on R&D, the world's highest; South Korea is 2nd at about 5%.

s: What is India's national target for Gross Expenditure on R&D?
x: The national target is GERD of 2% of GDP; India was at 0.84% in FY 2023-24.

s:
Consider the following statements about GERD as % of GDP:
1. India's GERD in FY 2023-24 was a 15-year high.
2. South Korea ranks 2nd in the world at about 5%.
3. China spends more than the USA as a share of GDP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India's 0.84% was a 15-year high and South Korea is 2nd at about 5%; China (about 2.4%) is below the USA (about 3.5%).

s: What was India's total R&D expenditure in FY 2023-24?
x: Total R&D funding nearly doubled from Rs 1.33 lakh crore in FY20 to Rs 2.45 lakh crore in FY24.

s: What was the approximate share of private industry in India's R&D expenditure in FY 2023-24?
x: Private industry accounted for 51.8% of R&D expenditure in FY 2023–24 and overtook public funding for the first time.

s: What was the private sector's share of India's GERD in 2020-21?
x: India's private share was about 36%, against about 70% in the USA and 76% in South Korea.

s: Which of the following is identified as a reason for the gap in private R&D spending in India?
o: Excessive private investment in basic research
x: Private risk aversion, weak lab–industry linkages and a shortage of deep-tech capital explain the gap; strong linkages or surplus capital would not.

s: Which agency had the largest share of central R&D spending in 2020-21 among DOS, ICAR, DAE and CSIR?
x: DOS had 18.4%, ahead of ICAR 12.4%, DAE 11.4% and CSIR 8.2%.

s: Which organisation has long been the largest spender in India's central R&D budget (31.6% in 2017-18)?
x: DRDO has long been the largest, with 31.6% of central R&D in 2017-18.

s: KIND-X is an innovation initiative between India and which country?
x: KIND-X is an India-Korea initiative, not India-Japan.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature associated with Startup India?
o: Self-certification under nine labour and environment laws
x: Startup India provides for winding up in 90 days, not 30 days. The Fund of Funds, three-year tax exemption and self-certification provisions are associated features.

s: On which date was Startup India launched?
x: Startup India was launched on 16 January 2016.

s: What is India's rank as a start-up hub, with 1.59 lakh DPIIT-recognised start-ups?
x: India is the third-largest start-up hub and had 1.59 lakh DPIIT-recognised start-ups according to the cited figure.

s: Within how many days can a start-up exit (close) under Startup India?
x: Startup India allows exit in 90 days, not 30.

s: What is India's rank in the Hurun Global Unicorn Index (Jun 2026), with 61 unicorns?
x: India is 4th with 61 unicorns.

s: Which institution in Hyderabad supports agri-start-up incubation?
x: MANAGE, Hyderabad supports agri-start-up incubation.

s: Under which initiative are Atal Tinkering Labs and incubators set up?
x: The Atal Innovation Mission (NITI Aayog) supports tinkering labs in schools and incubators.

s: Which body is the custodian of the RDI Scheme fund approved on 1 July 2025?
x: ANRF is the custodian of the Rs 1 lakh crore RDI fund.

s: What kind of research is the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), set up under the 2023 Act, meant to fund?
o: Basic as well as applied research
x: The ANRF Act, 2023 provides for funding both basic research and applied research.

s: What is the corpus of the RDI Scheme approved on 1 July 2025?
x: The RDI Scheme has Rs 1 lakh crore for private R&D in AI, quantum, biotech and energy.

s: In which year was NEERI, the CSIR laboratory at Nagpur, established?
x: NEERI was set up in 1958; 1977 is the founding year of CCMB, Hyderabad.

s: Where is CSIR's Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute (CSMCRI) located?
x: CSMCRI, established in 1954, is at Bhavnagar and works on salt, marine chemicals and desalination.

s: Which CSIR laboratory maintains national measurement standards and keeps Indian Standard Time?
x: The National Physical Laboratory (NPL), New Delhi, maintains national measurement standards and keeps Indian Standard Time.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: NPL, New Delhi, is associated with national measurement standards and Indian Standard Time. Microbial technology is associated with IMTECH, Chandigarh.

s: Where is the CSIR Institute of Microbial Technology (IMTECH), which holds the MTCC gene bank, located?
x: IMTECH is at Chandigarh (1984).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: NGRI (geophysics) is at Hyderabad; CFTRI is at Mysuru, NIO at Goa and CIMAP at Lucknow.

s:
Consider the following statements about CSIR laboratories:
1. CDRI and CIMAP are both located at Lucknow.
2. CSMCRI is located at Bhavnagar, Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: CDRI and CIMAP are both in Lucknow, and CSMCRI is at Bhavnagar, so both are correct.

s: Where is the CSIR Central Electrochemical Research Institute (CECRI) located?
x: CECRI is at Karaikudi, Tamil Nadu, not Kolkata.

s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of CSIR laboratories or centres located in Hyderabad?
o: NIGST, NIO Regional Centre and CCMB
x: CCMB, IICT and NGRI are CSIR laboratories or centres located in Hyderabad. CDFD and NIAB are DBT institutions, while INCOIS and NIGST are non-CSIR institutions.

s: Which institution has a Regional Centre at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh?
x: The NIO Regional Centre is at Visakhapatnam.

s: Which institution developed the world's first steel slag road?
x: CRRI built the steel slag road; NAL made HANSA-3 (NG) and CMERI the FAIR beam catcher.

s: NEERI-ZAR, developed by the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute, is primarily associated with which of the following?
x: NEERI-ZAR is a gravity water purifier that operates without electricity. It was developed by NEERI, Nagpur.

s: Methanol-to-DME technology, described as an LPG substitute, was scaled up by which laboratory?
x: NCL, Pune, developed and scaled up methanol-to-DME technology, with DME serving as an LPG substitute.

s: What is the distinction of HANSA-3 (NG)?
o: The first indigenously developed aircraft to be commercially manufactured in India
The first Indian satellite launched by a private company
The first aircraft jointly developed by India and DAE
The first Indian aircraft powered exclusively by hydrogen
x: HANSA-3 (NG) is the first indigenously developed aircraft to be commercially manufactured in India.

s: In which year was Saheli, the world's first non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill, introduced?
x: Saheli (centchroman) of CDRI, Lucknow came in 1991.

s: Which CSIR laboratory developed the beam catcher for the FAIR accelerator in Germany?
x: CMERI, Durgapur built the beam catcher for FAIR.

s: Which laboratory developed Saheli, the weekly oral contraceptive pill based on centchroman?
x: Saheli, a centchroman-based weekly oral contraceptive, was developed by the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow.

s: Dr. Niti Kumar, winner of the SERB Women Excellence Award 2020, works at which CSIR laboratory?
x: Dr. Niti Kumar of CSIR-CDRI, Lucknow received the SERB Women Excellence Award 2020.

s: After which bird is NAL's light transport aircraft 'Saras' named?
x: Saras, NAL's light transport aircraft that first flew in 2004, is named after the sarus crane.

s: Which CSIR laboratory developed 'Oneer', a low-cost drinking-water disinfection technology for rural areas?
x: Oneer was developed by CSIR-Indian Institute of Toxicology Research (IITR), Lucknow.

s: Which CSIR laboratory set up the zoo bio-bank at Darjeeling?
x: CCMB, Hyderabad set up the zoo bio-bank at Darjeeling that stores samples at -196 C.

s: Which CSIR laboratory, with CeNS Bengaluru, developed a piezoelectric polymer nanocomposite that produces electricity when pressed, for pressure sensing and energy harvesting?
x: CSIR-NCL Pune and CeNS Bengaluru made a PVDF-zirconia film that turns pressure (even footsteps) into electricity by the piezoelectric effect.

s: Into what does the 2026 MoU between Bullayya College, Visakhapatnam, and IICT aim to convert shrimp waste?
x: The MoU focuses on converting shrimp waste into chitin and glucosamine.

s: Under which department does Survey of India (NIGST, Hyderabad) function?
x: Survey of India is under DST.

s: The Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP), Lucknow, is an autonomous body of which department?
x: BSIP Lucknow is a DST autonomous institute, not a CSIR laboratory.

s: With whose vision was the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) founded in 1909?
x: IISc, Bengaluru, was founded in 1909 with the vision of Jamsetji Tata.

s: With which of the following is INCOIS, Hyderabad, mainly associated?
x: INCOIS was established in 1999 under MoES and is associated with tsunami early warning.

s: Under which ministry does INCOIS, Hyderabad, set up in 1999, function?
x: INCOIS (1999) is under MoES and provides tsunami warnings.

s: Who led India's first scientific expedition to the Arctic in August 2007?
x: India's first Arctic expedition (August 2007) was led by Rasik Ravindra of NCAOR, Goa.

s: What is the name of India's research station in the Arctic?
x: Himadri (2008) at Ny-Alesund, Svalbard is India's Arctic station; Maitri and Bharati are in Antarctica.

s: Where is Himadri, India's Arctic research station, located?
x: Himadri (2008) is at Ny-Alesund in Svalbard; Bharati (Larsemann Hills) and Maitri (Schirmacher Oasis) are in Antarctica.

s: Where is the National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS) located?
x: NCESS is at Akkulam, Thiruvananthapuram; it began as Kerala's Centre for Earth Science Studies in 1978.

s: Under which ministry has the National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS) functioned since 2014?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: Kerala's CESS became an autonomous institute of MoES from 1 January 2014 and was renamed NCESS.

s: What is the legal status of CSIR, set up in September 1942?
o: Autonomous body registered as a society
x: CSIR is an autonomous body registered as a society; it is not a statutory corporation.

s: In which year was BIRAC, DBT's not-for-profit company for biotech start-ups, set up?
x: BIRAC was set up in 2012, not 2008.

s: Which public sector undertaking is controlled by DSIR?
x: DSIR controls two PSUs, NRDC and CEL; CSIR is a research organisation, not a PSU.

s: In which year was the Department of Science and Technology (DST) set up?
x: DST was set up in 1971; DSIR came in 1985 and DBT in 1986.

s: In which year was the National Biotechnology Board (1982) upgraded into DBT?
x: The National Biotechnology Board of 1982 became DBT in 1986.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the leadership of CSIR?
o: The Prime Minister is its ex officio President
The Union S&T Minister is its ex officio President
The Director-General of CSIR is also Secretary, DSIR
The Director-General heads the Governing Body
x: The Prime Minister is CSIR's ex officio President; the Union S&T Minister is Vice-President.

s: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) has a network of how many national laboratories?
x: CSIR has 37 national laboratories, along with 39 outreach centres, 1 innovation complex and 3 units, and 3,300+ scientists. 39 is the number of outreach centres and 3,300 approximates its scientists; 27 is not a correct figure.

s: Who chairs BRIC, which integrates 14 DBT institutions?
o: Union Minister of Science and Technology
x: BRIC is chaired by the Union S&T Minister; the DBT Secretary is its ex officio Director-General.

s: Which other post does the Director-General of CSIR hold?
x: DG CSIR is also Secretary, DSIR, and heads the Governing Body.

s: Who is the ex officio Vice-President of CSIR?
o: Union Minister of Science and Technology
x: The Union S&T Minister is Vice-President; the Prime Minister is President.

s: Which one of the following is an institute of the Department of Biotechnology (DBT)?
o: Central Glass and Ceramic Research Institute
Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology
Centre of Innovative and Applied Bioprocessing
x: The Centre of Innovative and Applied Bioprocessing (CIAB), Mohali, is a DBT institute (APPSC-G2 2025). CFTRI, the Central Glass and Ceramic Research Institute and CCMB are CSIR laboratories.

s: Where is the Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics (CDFD), a DBT institute, located?
x: CDFD is in Hyderabad.

s: Which of the following DBT institutes is INCORRECTLY matched with its location?
x: NIPGR is in New Delhi; NIAB and CDFD are the DBT institutes in Hyderabad.

s: Which one of the following is an autonomous body under the Department of Science and Technology?
x: ARIES, Nainital is a DST autonomous body. NRDC and CEL are DSIR PSUs, and CDFD is a DBT institute.

s: For which international project is the Bose Institute, Kolkata (1917), India's nodal body?
x: The Bose Institute, a DST autonomous institute founded by J.C. Bose, is India's nodal body for FAIR.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: NM-ICPS was launched in 2018 with Rs 3,660 crore; Vigyan Jyoti is a DST scheme and DST is nodal for the RDI Scheme.

s: Who founded the Bose Institute, Kolkata, in 1917?
x: Jagadish Chandra Bose founded the Bose Institute in 1917; it is now an autonomous body of DST.

s: PRISM, PACE, BIRD-crf and A2K+ are components of the Umbrella Industrial R&D scheme of which department?
x: All four are components of DSIR's Umbrella Industrial R&D scheme.

s: Recognition by DSIR makes eligible in-house R&D centres and other recognised institutions for which of the following benefits?
o: Income tax and customs duty exemptions
x: DSIR recognition makes the recognised institutions eligible for income tax and customs duty exemptions.

s: When was DSIR set up?
x: DSIR was set up in January 1985; it controls CSIR, NRDC and CEL.

s: Which of the following public sector undertakings is under DSIR?
x: DSIR has two PSUs: NRDC and CEL (Central Electronics Limited).

s: What happened to SERB under the ANRF Act, 2023?
x: The ANRF Act, 2023 repealed the SERB Act, 2008 and subsumed SERB into ANRF; its schemes continue.

s: Whom does the SERB-POWER scheme support?
x: SERB-POWER is for women researchers; the SERB Overseas Fellowship is for the diaspora.

s: SERB, now subsumed into ANRF, was originally set up in 2008 as which type of body?
x: SERB was a statutory board under the SERB Act 2008.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its purpose?
x: Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship is for life sciences, not engineering.
